candidates.name: Service Charge Tribunal Corpus (England & Wales leasehold)
candidates.one_line: A downloadable folder of ~7,000 First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber) service-charge and leasehold-management decisions, issue-coded with outcome patterns, that turns a leaseholder's own ChatGPT/Claude into an assistant that argues from how the tribunal has ACTUALLY ruled instead of inventing case law.
candidates.buyer: Leaseholder (or informal residents' association / RMC director) facing a service-charge demand or a section 20 major-works bill they believe is unreasonable, preparing a s.27A application or a response to one. Property owners, so they can pay.
candidates.the_expensive_moment: A major-works bill or escalating service charge lands; the leaseholder either swallows it, pays a solicitor £250-400/hr, or self-represents at the FTT. Managing agents report leaseholders already firing AI-drafted challenges that FAIL because the model misapplies section 20 thresholds and blurs jurisdictions [VERIFIED - fetched https://building-trust.uk/directors-ai-disputes.html: 'sharp rise in AI-drafted complaints... multiple challenges per week on larger portfolios', failures from 'Consultation rules under Section 20 misapplied'].
candidates.money_at_stake: Average service charge in England & Wales is £2,405/yr (£2,801 London) per the Hamptons 2025 Service Charge Index [VERIFIED - fetched https://www.hamptons.co.uk/articles/2025-service-charge-index, HTTP 200]. Disputes typically span several years of charges plus one-off major-works bills of £10k+ per flat (the corpus decisions themselves document the sums). A successful s.27A challenge commonly moves £3k-£30k.
candidates.decision_body: First-tier Tribunal (Property Chamber - Residential Property), decisions published by HMCTS on GOV.UK
candidates.corpus_source: https://www.gov.uk/residential-property-tribunal-decisions with JSON API at https://www.gov.uk/api/search.json?filter_content_store_document_type=residential_property_tribunal_decision (paginatable); full decision PDFs on assets.publishing.service.gov.uk; Atom feed for updates
candidates.corpus_fetch_proof: Fetched the finder page (HTTP 200): 17,581 total decisions with category filters and an Atom feed. Fetched the gov.uk search API (HTTP 200): JSON returned total=17581 with title+link per decision, paginatable. Fetched the finder JSON with category filter leasehold-disputes-management (HTTP 200): total=6,995. Fetched a sample decision's content API (HTTP 200) which exposed the attachment URL, then downloaded the decision PDF from assets.publishing.service.gov.uk: HTTP 200, 496,578 bytes. Entire pipeline (enumerate -> resolve attachment -> download PDF) proven end-to-end.
candidates.corpus_size: 17,581 published decisions total; 6,995 in 'Leasehold disputes (management)' (service charges, management fees, s.20 consultation, s.20C costs) - all bulk-downloadable via the public gov.uk API, growing weekly (decisions dated July 2026 already present).
candidates.whats_in_the_folder: 00_START_HERE.md (how to load into a ChatGPT/Claude Project; information-only guardrails the AI must follow); 01_LAW.md (verified extracts: LTA 1985 ss.18-30, s.20C, SI 2003/1987 consultation thresholds, CLRA 2002, with legislation.gov.uk citations); 02_PROCEDURE.md (FTT application forms, fees, Property Chamber Rules 2013 incl. rule 14 lay representation, rule 13 costs regime); decisions/ (~2,000-3,000 curated decision extracts as text, in issue folders: management-fees/, insurance-commissions/, major-works-reasonableness/, s20-dispensation/, repairs-standard/, s20C-costs/); 03_OUTCOME_PATTERNS.md (per issue: N decisions, what panels allowed/disallowed, sums, each claim citing a file in decisions/); 04_EVIDENCE_CHECKLISTS.md (what documents panels actually relied on, drawn from the decisions); 05_WORKED_EXAMPLES.md (anonymised walkthroughs of real won and lost cases).
candidates.what_ai_invents_without_it: Unaided models know s.19 'reasonableness' exists but fabricate FTT case citations, invent the going rate for management fees per unit, misstate the £250/£100 s.20 thresholds and exemptions, and blur England/Wales/Scotland regimes - documented in the wild: managing agents describe AI-drafted challenges failing precisely on misapplied s.20 rules [VERIFIED - building-trust.uk fetch]. No model can say 'panels disallowed insurance commissions in N of M decisions like yours, here are the citations' - only the coded corpus can.
candidates.prompt_test: Best substitute prompt: 'You are an expert on UK leasehold service charge disputes. Using LTA 1985 s.19/s.20 and FTT case law, assess my service charge and draft a s.27A challenge.' This captures maybe 30-40% of the value: the statutory framework and letter structure are in the model. What it cannot supply: real decision citations (it invents FTT references), actual outcome patterns and quantum (what fee levels tribunals accept), evidence standards panels applied. Where the buyer is about to file at a tribunal, the fabricated-citation failure mode is exactly the catastrophic one.
candidates.volume_math: US$149 x ~50 sales/month = ~US$7,450/month (target R$30k net at ~US$7.4-8.3k). Feasibility: ~7,000 disputes reach decision; applications are a multiple of that; England has ~5 million leasehold homes and the Hamptons index made national press. Marketplace (Etsy/Gumroad) + SEO ('FTT service charge decisions database', 'challenge service charge tribunal') + written participation in r/LegalAdviceUK and LeaseholdKnowledge forum. 50 units/month is ~1.7/day from a market with zero direct competitors found.
candidates.channel: Gumroad + Etsy listing; SEO content site publishing free per-issue decision statistics as lead-in (the free stats page ranks, the coded corpus is the product); written answers in leasehold forums/Reddit. No calls, no face, English written only.
candidates.demand_evidence: FETCHED: building-trust.uk/directors-ai-disputes.html (HTTP 200) - managing agents report 'sharp rise in AI-drafted complaints... multiple challenges per week', proving leaseholders already reach for ChatGPT for exactly this task and fail on specifics [VERIFIED]. Corpus itself shows ~7,000 decided disputes in the category and fresh decisions weekly [VERIFIED via API]. Hamptons index coverage of record service charges drove national press in 2025-26 [VERIFIED fetch + BeBeez/Property118 coverage, PLAUSIBLE].
candidates.free_substitute_check: LEASE (Leasehold Advisory Service) - government-funded, 'gives free legal advice to leaseholders' [VERIFIED - fetched https://www.gov.uk/government/organisations/leasehold-advisory-service]. This is the real threat and the honest gap: LEASE explains the law and will discuss a case, but publishes no decision corpus, no outcome statistics, and does not sit inside the buyer's AI drafting sessions at 11pm. Citizens Advice covers generalities. The FTT publishes raw decisions but no synthesis. Nobody - including LEASE - supplies issue-coded outcome patterns with verified citations.
candidates.saturation_check: Searched Etsy and Gumroad (site: queries): only UK parking-ticket (PCN) appeal letter templates found; zero leasehold/service-charge AI packs, zero FTT corpus products [VERIFIED searches, literal top results: 'PCN Appeal Letters Bundle - Editable UK Templates', 'UK Parking Ticket Appeal Letter Template']. Adjacent product found: BundleCreator (hearing-bundle SOFTWARE for the Property Chamber) - different job. Not saturated.
candidates.reserved_activity_check: England & Wales, Legal Services Act 2007 s.12 [VERIFIED - fetched legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/29/section/12]: reserved activities are rights of audience, conduct of litigation, reserved instruments, probate, notarial, oaths - general legal advice/information is NOT reserved. FTT Property Chamber Rules 2013 rule 14 [VERIFIED - fetched legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1169/article/14/made]: 'A party may appoint a representative (whether legally qualified or not)' - self-representation and lay help are normal. Not immigration; not FCA claims-management (regulated sectors are personal injury, financial products, housing DISREPAIR, benefits, criminal injury, employment - service-charge reasonableness is none of these, and marketing must never frame it as 'compensation claims'). PERMITTED sentence: 'In this corpus, tribunal panels reduced or disallowed management fees in N of M comparable decisions; see decisions/management-fees/ for the citations.' FORBIDDEN sentence: 'Your service charge is unreasonable and you will win at the tribunal.' The folder supplies verified material; the buyer's own AI does the applying; Sol never sees a case (H7).
candidates.piracy_answer: Real exposure - leaseholders organise in blocks and forums. Mitigations: (1) the corpus goes stale visibly - new decisions publish weekly on the Atom feed, so the product ships as dated editions with quarterly refreshes and a cheap update path; a 2026 copy circulating in 2027 argues from superseded patterns; (2) buyer-email watermark line in every md file; (3) price already assumes one purchase per building being shared among its leaseholders - at £120-ish per BLOCK it undercuts one hour of a solicitor; (4) accept residual leakage. Honest note: the RAW corpus is public and a technical person could re-scrape it in an afternoon via the same API - the defensible layer is the issue-coding, outcome-counting and citation-verified synthesis across ~7,000 PDFs, which is weeks of pipeline work, not an afternoon.
candidates.weakest_link: LEASE offering free government-funded one-to-one leasehold advice is the strongest free substitute any candidate in this hunt faces; the product survives only because LEASE supplies advice-about-law while this supplies the decision-pattern corpus the buyer's AI needs to draft. Second: the raw decisions are public, so the moat is the coding layer plus update cadence, not the data itself.
candidates.evidence: [VERIFIED] legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/29/section/12 - general advice not reserved. [VERIFIED] legislation.gov.uk/uksi/2013/1169/article/14/made - lay representation. [VERIFIED] gov.uk finder + API, HTTP 200: 17,581 decisions, 6,995 in leasehold-management, sample PDF downloaded (496KB). [VERIFIED] hamptons.co.uk 2025 Service Charge Index: £2,405/yr average. [VERIFIED] building-trust.uk: leaseholders already using AI and failing on s.20 specifics. [VERIFIED] gov.uk: LEASE is government-funded free advice. [VERIFIED] Etsy/Gumroad searches: no competing product. [PLAUSIBLE] typical major-works bills £10k+/flat (documented within corpus decisions, not separately fetched).

candidates.name: Planning Appeal Decisions Corpus (England)
candidates.one_line: A folder of English planning appeal decisions coded by refusal reason (green belt, design, overlooking, highways), with outcome patterns per issue, turning a refused homeowner's or small developer's AI into a drafting assistant that argues from how Inspectors have actually decided - IF direct bulk access to decision letters is re-proven from a normal UK connection, which this environment could not do.
candidates.buyer: Small developer or homeowner refused planning permission, deciding between abandoning the scheme, paying a planning consultant £1,500-£5,000 for the appeal, or self-representing in a written-representations appeal (free to file).
candidates.the_expensive_moment: The refusal notice arrives. Appeal deadline (6 months, 12 weeks for householder) starts running. Consultant quotes £1,500-£5,000 [PLAUSIBLE - Checkatrade/MyBuilder cost guides via search]; the underlying loss (extension value, plot uplift) is tens to hundreds of thousands.
candidates.money_at_stake: Consultant substitution alone: £1,500-£5,000 typical appeal fees, fixed-fee services from £399 (myplanningappeal.co.uk) [PLAUSIBLE - search results, pages not individually fetched]. Underlying asset at stake far larger. NOTE: money-at-stake is verified only at PLAUSIBLE level for this candidate.
candidates.decision_body: The Planning Inspectorate (PINS), England - every appeal decision letter published with full reasoning
candidates.corpus_source: Old: acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk (Appeals Casework Portal). New (600XXXX refs): appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk, searchable only by reference or postcode. Metadata: PINS Appeals Casework dataset on data.gov.uk / opendatacommunities.org (5 rolling years, includes references that unlock the new service). Third-party: AppealBase (free, claims 100,000+ decisions), Appeal Finder (paid, 'all English planning appeals 2010-2026').
candidates.corpus_fetch_proof: HONEST FAILURE FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT: acp.planninginspectorate.gov.uk returned HTTP 504 on four attempts (curl and WebFetch, root and CaseSearch.aspx). appeal-planning-decision.service.gov.uk returned HTTP 200 (service is live) but decisions are gated behind reference/postcode search. opendatacommunities.org SPARQL returned 403 Access Denied. appealbase.com returned HTTP 429 twice. I retrieved ZERO decision letters. Countable secondary evidence fetched: appealfinder.co.uk LPA page (HTTP 200) states 10,071 s78 planning appeals + 4,142 householder + 1,672 enforcement + 585 LDC + 464 listed-building + 465 CAS issued in year ending 31 March 2025, coverage 'All English planning appeals 2010-2026'. The 504/429/403 pattern suggests proxy/geo blocking rather than nonexistence - two commercial businesses (Appeal Finder, AppealBase) are built on scraping this exact corpus - but per the H1 bar this candidate is UNPROVEN until decision letters are actually retrieved and counted from a UK consumer connection.
candidates.corpus_size: ~17,000 decisions/year across appeal types [VERIFIED count for 2024/25 via fetched Appeal Finder page]; 100,000+ decisions 2010-2026 [PLAUSIBLE - AppealBase's own claim, site unreachable from here]. Bulk-downloadability NOT proven from this environment.
candidates.whats_in_the_folder: 00_START_HERE.md (project setup + information-only guardrails); 01_FRAMEWORK.md (NPPF extracts, s.78 TCPA 1990, material considerations, verified citations); 02_PROCEDURE.md (written representations procedure, timetables, the April 2026 expedited householder procedure with its 250-word summary limit, costs-award rules); decisions/ (2,000-4,000 decision letters as text, in refusal-reason folders: green-belt/, design-character/, overlooking-amenity/, highways-parking/, overdevelopment/); 03_OUTCOME_PATTERNS.md (per refusal reason: allow/dismiss rates in the corpus, the arguments Inspectors accepted and rejected, citing files); 04_COSTS_AWARDS.md (when unreasonable behaviour costs are awarded); 05_WORKED_EXAMPLES.md.
candidates.what_ai_invents_without_it: Unaided models fabricate appeal reference numbers, invent Inspector reasoning patterns ('appeals on green belt openness succeed when...'), misquote NPPF paragraph numbers (renumbered repeatedly, incl. December 2024 revision), and cannot say how often a given refusal reason is overturned. The corpus supplies real allow/dismiss patterns per issue with citable decision letters.
candidates.prompt_test: 'You are a UK planning consultant. Draft my appeal statement against refusal for [reasons], citing NPPF and appeal precedent.' Captures ~40% of value: structure and general NPPF argumentation are known. It will confidently cite invented appeal decisions - which an Inspector will notice. The corpus's real outcome patterns per refusal reason and quotable genuine decisions are unavailable to any prompt.
candidates.volume_math: US$297 x ~26 sales/month = ~US$7,700/month. ~17,000 appeals decided/year plus a larger pool who were refused and are deciding whether to appeal; buyer is substituting a £1,500-£5,000 consultant so $297 is an easy yes. Channel maths sit in the paid-viable zone ($197+) if organic is slow.
candidates.channel: SEO ('planning appeal success rate green belt', 'write planning appeal statement'), Gumroad, written answers in self-build/extension forums (BuildHub, Reddit r/DIYUK); optional written cold outreach to architects who don't employ planners. No calls, no face.
candidates.demand_evidence: FETCHED: appealfinder.co.uk (HTTP 200) - a paid subscription business exists specifically selling planning-appeal-decision search to professionals, and its blog documents that PINS's new beta service HIDES appeals unless you know the reference/postcode, i.e. access friction is rising [VERIFIED]. AppealBase's existence as a second dedicated tool [PLAUSIBLE]. ~14,000+ appeals/yr filed by parties who each faced this exact decision [VERIFIED via fetched Appeal Finder counts].
candidates.free_substitute_check: Planning Portal - free PROCESS guidance on making/searching appeals, no outcome analysis [PLAUSIBLE]. PINS's own procedural guides - process only. AppealBase - FREE search of 100k+ decisions aimed at architects/consultants [PLAUSIBLE, unreachable from here]: the serious free substitute, though it is a search tool for professionals, not an outcome-coded corpus wired into a layperson's AI. Citizens Advice does not cover planning appeals substantively. No charity does the appeal-drafting job.

candidates.reserved_activity_check: Same LSA 2007 s.12 basis [VERIFIED]: planning is not even a reserved-activity-adjacent field - planning consultancy is an entirely unregulated profession, and appellants routinely self-represent in written representations (no hearing, so no right-of-audience question arises). Not immigration, not claims management. PERMITTED: 'In this corpus, Inspectors allowed N of M appeals where the sole refusal reason was rear-extension overlooking; the accepted arguments were X and Y - see decisions/overlooking/.' FORBIDDEN: 'Your appeal will succeed; submit this statement.' Buyer's AI applies the material; Sol never reviews a case.
candidates.piracy_answer: Same regime as candidate 1: dated quarterly editions (new decisions publish continuously), buyer-email watermarks, and acceptance of residual leakage; developer/architect buyers are business purchasers less prone to community-sharing than consumer groups. Raw decisions are public; the moat is refusal-reason coding + outcome statistics + the update cadence.
candidates.weakest_link: H1 is UNPROVEN: I retrieved zero decision letters from this environment (ACP 504 x4, AppealBase 429, opendatacommunities 403). Strong secondary evidence says the corpus exists and is scraped commercially, but per this hunt's own rule an uncounted corpus is worthless - do NOT build this before spending one day on a UK consumer connection proving bulk retrieval (metadata dataset -> references -> decision letters) and counting what comes back. Secondary risk: the April 2026 expedited householder procedure (250-word summaries, no full statement) shrinks the drafting surface for householder appeals - aim the product at full s78 appeals.

candidates.name: Recurso em 3 Dias — corpus TCU de licitações para o licitante inabilitado
candidates.one_line: A downloadable folder of 5,300+ curated TCU holdings on public-bid disqualification, indexed by rejection ground, that turns a losing bidder's own ChatGPT/Claude into a recurso-drafter that cites real acórdãos inside the 3-business-day legal deadline.
candidates.buyer: Brazilian SMEs that sell to government (pregão eletrônico bidders) at the moment they are inabilitadas/desclassificadas, plus the small consultorias de licitação that serve them. These firms already pay R$200-400/month for bid-alert tools (ConLicitação, Effecti), so willingness to pay for bidding tooling is proven.
candidates.the_expensive_moment: Lei 14.133/2021 art. 165: after disqualification the bidder must manifest intent to appeal IMMEDIATELY in the session (sob pena de preclusão) and file the razões within 3 dias úteis [VERIFIED - planalto.gov.br text fetched]. A specialist administrative-law lawyer cannot usually be found, briefed and paid within that window; ConLicitação's own free guide tells the disqualified company to 'consult a lawyer specialized in bids' [VERIFIED - fetched conlicitacao.com.br article, HTTP 200]. The buyer needs a competent recurso tonight, and their bare AI fabricates the citations.
candidates.money_at_stake: The contract they were about to win. PNCP public API [VERIFIED]: I fetched pncp.gov.br/api/consulta/v1/contratos for a single day (2025-06-02), HTTP 200: 13,910 contracts signed in one day, with per-contract values in the response (first page samples R$5.999 to R$186.932; valorGlobal field per contract). Even a small municipal fornecimento contract is worth tens to hundreds of thousands of reais - versus a US$197 folder.
candidates.decision_body: Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) - whose acórdãos, súmulas and enunciados are THE authority cited in licitação recursos nationwide - plus the statute (Lei 14.133/2021) and its own curated digests (Jurisprudência Selecionada, Informativo de Licitações e Contratos).
candidates.corpus_source: Official TCU open-data bulk CSVs at https://sites.tcu.gov.br/dados-abertos/jurisprudencia/arquivos/ (index: jurisprudencia-arquivos.csv) and JSON API https://dados-abertos.apps.tcu.gov.br/api/acordao/recupera-acordaos
candidates.corpus_fetch_proof: All fetched, all HTTP 200: (1) API recupera-acordaos?inicio=0&quantidade=5 returned live JSON - acórdãos 2077-2081/2026, session of 05/08/2026, two days before today. (2) Index CSV jurisprudencia-arquivos.csv (5.9 KB): 35 full-text yearly CSVs, acordao-completo-1992.csv through 2026, ~7.9 GB total. (3) jurisprudencia-selecionada.csv downloaded in full (116.8 MB): 17,729 curated theses counted by key; 3,342 with AREA='Licitação' and 1,108 with AREA='Contrato Administrativo' counted by field match - each row has ENUNCIADO, EXCERTO, TEMA/SUBTEMA, acórdão number/year/colegiado, REFERENCIALEGAL. (4) informativo-lc.csv downloaded in full (7.78 MB): 1,991 Informativo de Licitações e Contratos entries counted (through issue 531/2026). (5) acordao-completo-resumo.csv downloaded (55.3 MB): 35,061 plain-language acórdão summaries counted. (6) sumula.csv listed in the same index (800 KB).
candidates.corpus_size: 4,450 curated licitação/contract theses + 1,991 informativo holdings + súmulas + 35,061 AI summaries + full text of every TCU acórdão 1992-2026 (~7.9 GB, 35 files) - all bulk-downloadable as CSV from the official site, no auth, no scraping. The product ships the curated ~7,000-document layer, not the raw gigabytes.
candidates.whats_in_the_folder: 00-instrucoes.md (drafting protocol for the buyer's AI: intake questions, deadline rules, citation-verification rule 'never cite an acórdão not present in this corpus'); 01-lei-14133-anotada.md (arts. 164-168 full text + pregão flow, preclusão trap, contrarrazões deadlines); 02-enunciados-habilitacao.md through 02-enunciados-por-motivo (the 3,342 Licitação theses split by rejection ground: atestado de capacidade técnica, quantitativos mínimos, exequibilidade da proposta, saneamento de vícios formais, ME/EPP benefits, registro cadastral - each with enunciado, acórdão cite, legal reference); 03-enunciados-contratos.md (1,108 theses); 04-informativo-lc-digest.md (1,991 entries, newest first); 05-sumulas-tcu.md; 06-anatomia-do-recurso.md (structure of intenção de recurso, razões, contrarrazões, pedido de reconsideração - generic anatomy, not case advice); 07-indice-mestre.md (rejection ground -> theses -> how often TCU sides with the bidder).
candidates.what_ai_invents_without_it: Asked for TCU jurisprudence on, e.g., restrictive atestado requirements, a bare model produces the real Súmula 263 plus invented acórdão numbers with fabricated quotes, asserts a nonexistent 'entendimento pacífico', and gets deadlines wrong (mixes Lei 8.666's 5 days with 14.133's 3 dias úteis; knows nothing of 2026 changes - LC 227/2026 just rewrote Decreto 70.235 deadlines, proving how fast this moves). A pregoeiro can disprove a fake citation in 30 seconds on pesquisa.apps.tcu.gov.br, which kills the recurso's credibility exactly when the money is on the table.
candidates.prompt_test: Best substitute prompt: 'Redija um recurso administrativo contra inabilitação em pregão por atestado de capacidade técnica insuficiente, fundamentado na Lei 14.133/2021 e na jurisprudência do TCU.' Honestly captures ~60% of the value: the drafting structure, formalismo-moderado arguments and one or two real súmulas come out fine. What it cannot supply: verifiable acórdão citations on the buyer's exact rejection ground, the frequency evidence ('TCU has held X in N decisions since 2020'), and current-year holdings - the corpus's Informativo 531/2026 entries postdate any model's cutoff.
candidates.volume_math: US$197 x 40 sales/month = US$7,880 ≈ R$30k target. TAM sanity: PNCP recorded 13,910 signed contracts in ONE day [VERIFIED]; every pregão produces losing bidders and disqualification events daily, so 40 buyers/month is a trivial penetration of a standing national flow. Support load at 40 units/month is absorbable solo.
candidates.channel: Organic search in Portuguese on the crisis queries ('fui inabilitado no pregão', 'recurso administrativo licitação prazo') where current competition is law-firm blogs; Hotmart marketplace listing; and written cold outreach (e-mail) to companies recorded as losing/disqualified bidders in public PNCP/compras.gov.br session records - a self-refreshing, perfectly-timed prospect list. No calls, no audience, all written Portuguese.
candidates.demand_evidence: Portuguese-language evidence fetched/searched: JusBrasil article 'Fui inabilitado no pregão, e agora?'; ConLicitação's free guide 'O que fazer quando sua empresa é inabilitada em uma licitação?' [VERIFIED - fetched, HTTP 200, advises the 3-day recurso and hiring a specialist lawyer]; multiple law firms SEO-farming the same query ('Fui Inabilitado na Licitação: Guia Prático em 5 Passos' - brunocarvalhoadv.com; galvaoesilva.com; paschoalinberger.adv.br) - lawyers compete for this traffic because the buyers pay.
candidates.free_substitute_check: Sebrae: free courses 'Licitações Sem Mistérios' and 'Cartilha do Comprador' - they teach HOW TO PARTICIPATE and use compras.gov.br, not how to win a recurso with authority [VERIFIED titles via search]. TCU itself: free search portal and these very CSVs - free raw material, zero curation into an AI-usable, ground-indexed folder. ConLicitação/Effecti: free blog guides as marketing for bid-alert subscriptions; their advice at the critical moment is 'hire a lawyer'. Zênite/Sollicita sell expensive jurisprudence subscriptions to PUBLIC BUYERS (órgãos), not to bidders. Nobody gives away the assembled, indexed decision corpus doing the whole job.
candidates.saturation_check: Searched Hotmart/Gumroad/open web in Portuguese. Found only AI TRAINING for humans, mostly aimed at public servants: 'Oficina Prática de Licitações com IA - VIP' (Hotmart); 'INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL EM LICITAÇÕES E CONTRATOS: Do Iniciante ao Avançado' (Eleva Soluções Públicas); Grupo Incap live training 'Inteligência Artificial (ChatGPT) nas compras e contratações'; free PDF 'Licitações do Futuro: como criar agentes personalizados no ChatGPT' (Ronny Charles). No decision-corpus folder product, no bidder-side AI product found. Not saturated.
candidates.reserved_activity_check: Administrative, not judicial. Lei 8.906/94 art. 1º, I reserves postulation 'a qualquer órgão do PODER JUDICIÁRIO' only (with ADI 1.127 annotation) - administrative bodies are not the Judiciary [VERIFIED - planalto text fetched]. Lei 9.784/99 art. 3º, IV: lawyer assistance in administrative process is 'facultativa' [VERIFIED]. Lei 14.133 art. 164: 'Qualquer pessoa é parte legítima para impugnar edital'; art. 165 gives the recurso to the licitante itself [VERIFIED]. The reserved line is art. 1º, II 'consultoria, assessoria e direção jurídicas' - case-specific advice. PERMITTED: 'Esta pasta reúne 3.342 enunciados oficiais do TCU sobre licitação, organizados por motivo de inabilitação, com a citação de cada acórdão.' FORBIDDEN: 'Analisamos seu caso: sua inabilitação foi ilegal e seu recurso será provido' (case opinion), and any per-client drafting service or advertising 'assessoria jurídica em licitações'. The buyer's own AI applies the material; Sol never sees a case (H7).
candidates.piracy_answer: Accept leakage and price the freshness: TCU publishes new acórdãos weekly and the Informativo biweekly (issue 531/2026 already), and the law itself moved mid-2026 (LC 227/2026), so a 6-month-old pirated copy visibly decays - sell as dated edition + 12 months of update files. Watermark each buyer's name/CNPJ into the file headers. The buyer profile also limits sharing: a company in a 3-day emergency buys the current official version rather than hunting a Telegram copy.
candidates.weakest_link: The raw corpus is free and officially bulk-published, so the moat is only the curation layer (rejection-ground taxonomy, AI instruction file, updates) - a competent competitor, including incumbents like ConLicitação, could replicate it in weeks; and the purchase is episodic crisis-driven (low LTV), so revenue depends on continuously winning the 'fui inabilitado' search moment against law-firm SEO.

candidates.name: ET Respondent's Corpus - the small employer's Employment Tribunal defence library
candidates.one_line: A folder of curated full-text Employment Tribunal judgments plus a pattern digest built from 133,287 published decisions, so a micro-employer's own AI can draft an ET3 response and hearing preparation grounded in how tribunals have actually ruled - instead of hallucinating case law.
candidates.buyer: UK micro/small employer (1-30 staff, no HR department, no retained solicitor) who has just received an ET1 claim form and has 28 days to file an ET3 response or face default judgment.
candidates.the_expensive_moment: An ET1 arrives from ACAS/the tribunal office. The employer has 28 days to file a legally coherent ET3 'grounds of resistance'. A solicitor quotes £6,000-£30,000 to defend; doing nothing risks default judgment and an uncapped discrimination award. This is the single moment they search 'et3 response example'.
candidates.money_at_stake: Defending a claim costs an employer £6,000-£30,000+ in legal fees (British Chambers of Commerce average ~£8,500); median unfair dismissal award ~£6,746 with maximum £179,124, and discrimination awards are uncapped [PLAUSIBLE - davidsonmorris.com/average-cost-of-employment-tribunal-to-employer, harperjames.co.uk/article/cost-of-employment-tribunals-for-employers, Brodies LLP tribunal awards summary, surfaced via search 2026-08-07; primary MOJ tables not fetched].
candidates.decision_body: Employment Tribunals (England, Wales and Scotland) - first-instance judgments with written reasons, published by HMCTS on GOV.UK since February 2017.
candidates.corpus_source: https://www.gov.uk/employment-tribunal-decisions - with a machine-readable JSON API at https://www.gov.uk/api/search.json?filter_content_store_document_type=employment_tribunal_decision (paginated), each record resolving via /api/content/ to a full-text PDF on assets.publishing.service.gov.uk.
candidates.corpus_fetch_proof: [VERIFIED] I fetched https://www.gov.uk/api/search.json?filter_content_store_document_type=employment_tribunal_decision&count=0 - HTTP 200, total 133,287 decisions. Faceted counts also fetched: unfair-dismissal 59,839; disability-discrimination 22,057. I then fetched one content item (Johal v N Lincs & Goole NHS Trust 2600557/2024) via /api/content/ - HTTP 200 - and it exposed the direct full-judgment PDF URL on assets.publishing.service.gov.uk. The whole corpus is enumerable and downloadable by trivially paginating one JSON API.
candidates.corpus_size: 133,287 published decisions (counted 2026-08-07), filterable by ~40 claim-type facets via the same API; roughly 14,000 new decisions/year. Bulk-downloadable: yes - JSON API pagination plus direct PDF asset URLs, no auth, Open Government Licence. Nobody rebuilds the curated subset plus the cross-decision pattern digest in an afternoon; the digest alone requires machine-reading thousands of PDFs.
candidates.whats_in_the_folder: (1) instructions.md - project instructions defining the AI's role, the information-not-advice boundary, and how to use the corpus; (2) /judgments/ - ~600-800 curated full-text judgments with reasons, chosen for small-employer fact patterns across unfair dismissal (misconduct, redundancy, SOSR), disability discrimination, wages and whistleblowing; (3) index.csv - case number, year, claim types, outcome, key issue tags for every included judgment; (4) patterns.md - the crown jewel: a digest built by machine-reading thousands of decisions ('in N misconduct dismissals by employers under 50 staff, the dismissal failed where no appeal was offered in X% of cases, e.g. [12 citations]'); (5) rates-and-limits.md - current Vento bands, statutory caps, ACAS uplift rules, all dated; (6) procedure.md - ET Rules of Procedure 2024, ET3 mechanics, deposit orders, strike-out, schedule of loss anatomy; (7) et3-anatomy.md - structure of grounds of resistance reverse-engineered from how judgments recite winning and losing defences.
candidates.what_ai_invents_without_it: Unaided models fabricate ET case names and case numbers wholesale (first-instance ET judgments are barely in training data and not on Find Case Law), state out-of-date or invented Vento band figures and statutory caps (these change every April), misstate the ACAS Code uplift and Polkey mechanics, and invent procedural rules from the superseded 2013 Rules instead of the 2024 Rules. A UK litigant was already criticised in court for AI-fabricated citations, so the failure mode is documented [PLAUSIBLE].
candidates.prompt_test: Best substitute: 'You are a UK employment law assistant. Browse gov.uk/employment-tribunal-decisions, find unfair dismissal judgments against small employers similar to my facts, and use them plus ACAS guidance to draft my ET3.' Honest result: with browsing the model can open perhaps 3-8 PDFs before context runs out, cannot compute patterns across thousands, and reverts to fabricating citations and rates. It captures maybe 30% of the value - the generic structure - and none of the 'tribunals have decided your exact issue N times, here is the pattern with citations' layer.
candidates.volume_math: US$397 x 20 sales/month = US$7,940 ≈ R$30k net target. ~14,000 decisions published/year implies well over 1,000 new claims served on employers every month (receipts exceed published decisions); every respondent has a hard 28-day deadline. 20 sales/month = under 2% of monthly new respondents, of whom a large share are unrepresented micro-employers balking at £8,500 average legal fees. £310 vs £8,500 is a rational purchase.

candidates.reserved_activity_check: Legal Services Act 2007 s.12 [VERIFIED - fetched legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/2007/29/section/12]: reserved activities are rights of audience, conduct of litigation, reserved instruments, probate, notarial acts, oaths - general legal advice/information is NOT reserved. Employment Tribunals Act 1996 s.6 [VERIFIED - fetched legislation.gov.uk/ukpga/1996/17/section/6]: a person may appear in person or be represented by 'any other person whom he desires to represent him'. Critical perimeter: FCA claims-management regulation covers services to CLAIMANTS pursuing employment-related claims - so the product targets RESPONDENT employers only, who are not making a claim, keeping it entirely outside CMC scope. Permitted: 'Tribunals have considered dismissal without an appeal hearing in 214 published decisions; in these 170 the dismissal was found unfair - citations attached.' Forbidden: 'Your dismissal of Sarah was fair and you will win' or any claimant-side 'we will get you compensation' framing.

Per-buyer watermarking of index.csv row order and invisible markers in patterns.md identifies leakers. The buyer is a business in a legal dispute - the least community-sharing buyer type there is. Money-at-stake figures rest on reputable law-firm summaries of MOJ data, not the MOJ tables themselves - fetch those before build.
candidates.evidence: H1 [VERIFIED]: 133,287 decisions counted via live API, per-facet counts confirmed, one full-text PDF resolved - the strongest corpus proof in this project. H4 [VERIFIED from primary legislation as above]. Demand [VERIFIED via fetched autocomplete]. H2/H3 checked by name with results reported. H9 [PLAUSIBLE, multiple concordant law-firm sources].
